item.title: Lagos Court Denies KC Luxury Bail, Orders Speedy Trial - Crime
item.description:
Justice Musa Kakaki of the Federal High Court in Lagos on Wednesday refused to grant bail to businessman and social media influencer Afolabi Michael Kazeem, popularly known as KC Luxury, over alleged 184.5kg cocaine trafficking and money laundering.

The judge held that the defence had failed to establish special circumstances to warrant bail on medical grounds, insisting that the application lacked sufficient evidence to justify the defendant’s release.

The jud...
item.content:encoded:
Justice Musa Kakaki of the Federal High Court in Lagos on Wednesday refused to grant bail to businessman and social media influencer Afolabi Michael Kazeem, popularly known as KC Luxury, over alleged 184.5kg cocaine trafficking and money laundering.

The judge held that the defence had failed to establish special circumstances to warrant bail on medical grounds, insisting that the application lacked sufficient evidence to justify the defendant’s release.

The judge further held that there was no medical certificate to warrant the court granting him bail.

“There is no medical certificate to warrant the court to grant him bail,” Kakaki ruled.

“If there is a special medical need for the first defendant, where a suspect claims an illness, an expert in the field would have given an explanation,” he said.

Kakaki, however, directed the Ikoyi Custodial Centre to grant Kazeem unrestricted access to doctors and medical experts for the treatment of any health condition.

The judge also ordered an accelerated hearing of the case, adjourning it until November 2, 2026, for the commencement of the trial.

At the last proceedings on Friday, Kazeem was brought to the court premises in an ambulance while receiving oxygen.

His counsel, Emefo Etudo, had urged the court to grant him bail to enable him to receive specialised medical treatment at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital.

Etudo argued that Kazeem’s health had deteriorated, particularly following the collapse of his lungs, which he said was disclosed by the Police Hospital, Falomo.

Opposing the application, prosecution counsel, Abu Ibrahim, argued that the medical evidence presented by the defence did not sufficiently justify the defendant’s release.

“Your Lordship looked at the application. The ailment is the same. It is the same asthma. But maybe it has become acute; the character and the ailment are the same,” Ibrahim said.

He added that the defence had not presented a medical document from LUTH showing that the hospital could not manage Kazeem’s condition.

When the case was called on Wednesday, a correctional officer from the Ikoyi Custodial Centre, Adeleye Akin, informed the court that Kazeem was still at the Police Hospital in Falomo.

Delivering his ruling, Kakaki said he had considered the bail application, the court records and the submissions of counsel on both sides.

The judge held that an applicant seeking bail must provide sufficient and cogent evidence to establish why the court should grant the request.

He also reviewed the medical evidence previously presented by the defence, including exhibits AK5, AK6 and AK8, which he said contained photographs of an individual lying on a hospital bed receiving treatment.

Kakaki recalled that in his ruling delivered on October 2, 2026, the court had noted a medical officer’s recommendation that Kazeem be assessed by a consultant respiratory physician or pulmonologist to evaluate his condition, optimise his treatment and prevent further acute episodes.

The judge said the recommendation did not establish that the defendant was suffering from an untreated illness.

He said, “Having gone through the records of the court and compared the ruling of October 2, 2026, I hereby discountenance all the exhibits.”

Addressing the defence’s argument that Kazeem needed specialised treatment at LUTH, Kakaki questioned the claim that the defendant could not be treated in a Nigerian hospital when the same application sought his release to enable him to receive treatment at the teaching hospital.

“Is it not ironic that the facility he said he cannot be treated in is the same LUTH he wants him to go to for specialised treatment?”

The judge also said the defence had failed to demonstrate any change in circumstances to justify a fresh bail application.

“However, changes in the circumstances were not disclosed.”

He recalled that on October 16, 2026, the court had ordered that Kazeem be remanded in a custodial centre.

“There is an inability to show special circumstances to warrant bail. I hereby discountenance it in the present application,” he said.

Kakaki further held that a claim of illness requiring specialist treatment should be supported by an expert’s assessment explaining the defendant’s condition.

“There was nothing stopping the Correctional Centre from calling an expert to attend to the first defendant, or using the first defendant’s doctor if he had one,” the judge said.

Refusing the application, Kakaki said, “The application is not granted; bail is refused to the first defendant. The case will proceed to an accelerated hearing.

“Where there is any health issue, the Correctional Centre shall give unfettered access to a doctor or expert for his treatment.”

Kazeem is standing trial alongside Boniface Freeman Ochoche Sule and Ikechukwu Ekugo Patriarch over alleged 184.5kg cocaine trafficking and money laundering.

The case was adjourned until November 2, 2026, for the commencement of the trial.

item.description:

In a petition dated after Thursday’s encounter, Edo Queens asked CAF to declare the continuation of the final, played on 29 October, null and void, citing alleged irregularities in the venue change, m...
item.content:encoded:
Nigeria Women’s Football League champions Edo Queens have petitioned the Confederation of African Football (CAF), seeking to overturn their 3-2 extra-time defeat to Ghanaian champions Ampem Darkoa Ladies in the disputed final of the 2026 WAFU-B Women’s Champions League

In a petition dated after Thursday’s encounter, Edo Queens asked CAF to declare the continuation of the final, played on 29 October, null and void, citing alleged irregularities in the venue change, match arrangements and eligibility of players.

The Nigerian club also urged the continental governing body to suspend confirmation of the regional qualification slot for the CAF Women’s Champions League pending the determination of its complaint.

The fresh protest follows a contentious sequence of decisions that overturned Edo Queens’ initial victory in the regional final and gave both teams another opportunity to contest the title.

How Ampem Darkoa Won
Ampem Darkoa secured the WAFU-B title after defeating Edo Queens 3-2 following extra time in the rescheduled conclusion to the final.
The encounter followed the original meeting between the sides on 5 September in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, which ended 2-2 after 90 minutes.

Edo Queens subsequently won the penalty shoot-out 4-1 and initially appeared to have secured the regional championship and qualification for the continental competition.
However, Ampem Darkoa challenged the outcome, prompting CAF’s Organising Committee to rule on 26 September that the penalty shoot-out had no sporting effect.

The decision, subsequently upheld by the CAF Appeal Board on 16 October, directed that the match resume from the beginning of extra time with the score still at 2-2.

When play eventually continued on Thursday, Ampem Darkoa struck the decisive blow just two minutes into extra time to secure the 3-2 victory.

The Ghanaian champions thereby claimed the WAFU-B title and the zone’s qualification place for the 2026 CAF Women’s Champions League.

The triumph marks Ampem Darkoa’s return to the continental competition for the second time in their history, having previously featured in 2023 in Côte d’Ivoire.

item.content:encoded:
2027:If they kidnap our children, I will enter the bush with them—Presidential candidate Peter Obi vows to personally join rescue efforts if elected President

Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has vowed to take a hands-on approach to insecurity, saying he would personally join efforts to rescue Nigerians abducted by criminals if elected president in 2027.

Speaking at a town hall meeting in Enugu State on Thursday, Obi said Nigeria needed a president who would be active, accountable and directly involved in tackling the country’s challenges.

“If there is a general bush, I will be in that bush with them,” he declared.

“As President of Nigeria, I will unite Nigeria. As President of Nigeria, I will secure Nigeria. We will deal with insecurity. I will not be president and somebody will k+dnap our children; we will enter the bush together.”


Obi, who has been touring different states ahead of the 2027 elections, said Nigerians were battling hunger, unemployment and insecurity.

“Today, our country is suffering. Today, people are hungry. Our children do not have employment. Today, Nigeria is not secured,” he said.

He also challenged President Bola Tinubu to tour the country and explain his administration’s performance, including how borrowed funds have been spent.

“Our President must come and account for three years he’s been in office. He cannot stay in Abuja, and want us to vote for him. No! This job requires energy, requires travel,” Obi said.

“As President of Nigeria, we will put emergency on corruption. People must stop stealing public money. Public money must be used for public good,”

he said.

Obi urged Nigerians not to support him based on ethnicity, insisting, “Don’t vote for me, because I’m an Igbo man. Please, I’m asking for your vote because I’m the most qualified to be President of Nigeria.”

.

In a statement on Wednesday, the FCT Police Public Relatio...
item.content:encoded:
The Federal Capital Territory Police Command has arrested a Deputy Superintendent of Corps with the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Onoja Samuel, for allegedly firing shots into the air during a confrontation with traders at a market in the Kubwa area of Abuja.

According to the police, Samuel had gone to the market armed with a pistol following reports that some traders had assaulted his wife.

In a statement on Wednesday, the FCT Police Public Relations Officer, SP Josephine Adeh, said operatives attached to the Kubwa Police Division were promptly deployed to the scene and arrested the suspect after disarming him.

“On 25th October, 2026, at about 1:50 pm, a distress call was received at Kubwa Police Division reporting that an unidentified man, armed with a pistol, was firing sporadically into the air at a market in Kubwa, Abuja.

“Upon receipt of the report, Police operatives attached to Kubwa Division were promptly deployed to the scene. Following concerted efforts, the suspect was successfully disarmed and arrested.

“Preliminary investigations identified the suspect as one Onoja Samuel, a Deputy Superintendent of Corps with the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps.

“Further findings revealed that the suspect had gone to the market armed with a pistol following reports that some traders had assaulted his wife. During an ensuing argument with the traders, he fired several shots into the air, ” Adeh said.

The police spokesperson said a CZ pistol and 17 rounds of live 9mm ammunition were recovered from the suspect during his arrest.

She added that the NSCDC officer remained in police custody and would be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigations.

The Commissioner of Police in the FCT, Ahmed Sanusi, urged personnel of sister security agencies to exercise restraint and notify the police divisions responsible for areas where they intend to conduct authorised operations.

“Operatives of sister security agencies are urged to exercise restraint and notify the Police Divisions responsible for the areas in which they intend to conduct sanctioned operations within the FCT, to ensure proper coordination and prevent avoidable clashes,” he said.

Abosede Ayeni, Tantalizers

Ayeni is the founder of Tantalizers Plc, one of Nigeria’s early home-grown quick-service restaurant brands. Before going into food, she worked at Lever Brothers Nigeria and Senkay Nigeria.

She started Tantalizers in 1997, building a brand that brought African menus into the QSR format. The company also runs outdoor and industrial catering, and earns revenue from both company-owned and franchised outlets.

Tantalizers listed on the Nigerian Stock Exchange in 2008, which set it apart in a sector dominated by private operators. The listing brought public-market scrutiny, and the company has had to contend with tougher competition and years of financial pressure. In 2024 it got a new majority shareholder, Food Specialties, and a reconstituted board. It has since reported a return to profit for the 2025 financial year.

item.content:encoded:
2027: Gbenga Hashim Gains Ground in Osun as Residents reject Adeleke’s Tinubu Alliance

Support for Accord Party presidential candidate, Dr Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, is becoming a feature of political discussions in Osun State, as some radio callers and social media commentators question Governor Ademola Adeleke’s decision to support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.

Callers on radio stations, including Diamond FM, Unique FM and King FM, have reportedly favoured Hashim’s presidential agenda amid the debate over Adeleke’s political alignment.

Meanwhile, videos circulating on TikTok and Facebook show content creators identified as Almaruf, Doki Dorcas, The God, Unusual Challenges, etc expressing support for Hashim and criticising the governor’s position.

In one of the videos, Doki Dorcas urged Osun residents to support Hashim’s presidential ambition. In another, Almaruf argued that voters who supported Accord during the governorship election should not abandon their earlier political choice to return to the APC.

“We rejected APC by voting for Accord, and we won’t return to our vomit,” Almaruf said in the video.


The conversation has also reportedly extended beyond Osun, with social media influencers in Oyo, Kwara and Lagos promoting Hashim’s presidential agenda.

Supporters interpret these activities as signs of growing engagement with Hashim's candidacy across the Southwest.

The Southwest mobilisation effort also has a stated numerical target. Alhaji Abass Olaniyi, the Southwest Coordinator of the Gbenga Hashim Solidarity Movement, has set a target of attracting three million votes for Hashim across the region.

For now, the dispute over Adeleke’s alignment with Tinubu has opened a wider conversation about party loyalty, political leadership and voters’ freedom to make independent choices in the 2027 presidential election.

item.content:encoded:
It's a breaking news, binance is hacked and 6 billion USD stolen.

Binance says $6.3bn stolen in biggest crypto heist in history

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has said that about $6.3bn in funds have been stolen in a “security incident” that looks to be the biggest crypto heist in history.

The world’s largest crypto exchange said on Thursday that it had suspended all deposits and withdrawals and that about $3bn in funds had been frozen following the apparent hacking.

Binance said an initial investigation suggested that a hacker had been able to make unauthorised transactions after gaining access to an engineer’s compromised laptop.

The company said it would cover all losses, adding that user funds were “safe”.

“Our teams are working around the clock to resolve this issue safely and thoroughly,” Binance said in a statement to Al Jazeera.

“We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice.”

The company added that it would share a “detailed” technical post-mortem once investigations were complete.

Changpeng Zhao, Binance’s founder and largest shareholder, said earlier that the exchange appeared to have been hacked.

TRM, a blockchain intelligence firm, said in a report that it assessed with “high confidence” that the attack was carried out by North Korea’s hacking unit TraderTraitor, which investigators have linked to the Lazarus Group.
Ari Redbord, TRM’s global head of policy, described the attack as “unprecedented” and a “watershed”.

“When North Korea steals at this scale, the money funds weapons proliferation and other destabilising activity. That makes this a global security issue, not just a crypto theft,” Redbord told Al Jazeera.

The price of Bitcoin, the world’s most popular cryptocurrency, fell about 5 percent following the heist, dropping below $77,000.

“Binance is one of the largest centralised exchanges, and so a blow to confidence in them risks shocking confidence to many retail investors, which could dampen prices of crypto assets,” Sean Foley, an expert in crypto markets at Macquarie University in Sydney, told Al Jazeera.

Foley said the attack highlighted the risks of centralised exchanges and could spur more traders to use decentralised alternatives.

“Any assets held at a centralised exchange are only as safe as the exchange itself, and the larger the exchange’s holdings, the larger a target it becomes,” Foley said.

The Binance hacking dwarfs the previous record for a crypto theft, set in 2025 when North Korean state-backed Lazarus Group carried out a $1.5bn heist on Bybit.

Cybercriminals stole $2.87bn in crypto assets in nearly 150 hacking incidents in 2025, according to the 2026 Crypto Crime Report produced by TRM.

Binance, founded in China by Zhao in 2017, has about $155bn in assets under management, more than any other exchange, according to CoinMarketCap.

item.content:encoded:
UPTH RESPONDS TO VIRAL VIDEO, DEFENDS HOSPITAL SERVICES

Previous thread
https://www.nairaland.com/8773746/man-alleges-upth-denied-brother

The University of Port Harcourt Teaching Hospital (UPTH) has dismissed allegations in a viral video concerning its services, defending the availability of medical equipment while acknowledging challenges relating to electricity supply and staff shortages.

In a press release dated October 29, 2026, the hospital's Public Relations Officer, Mr. Kem Daniel-Elebiga, and Head of the SERVICOM Unit, Mr. Efere Azubalu, said the Accident and Emergency Department had no record identifying the patient featured in the video. The management also dismissed claims that a sphygmomanometer, used to measure blood pressure, was unavailable, insisting that decisions on medical procedures rested with qualified physicians.

On electricity supply, the hospital said power availability had improved following efforts by its Chief Medical Director, Professor Chituru Godwill Orluwene, to secure its inclusion in the Federal Government's Energising Education Off-Grid Solar Project at the University of Port Harcourt. However, it acknowledged that weather-related fluctuations and rehabilitation works sometimes caused temporary power interruptions, with critical areas given priority before full supply was restored.

The management also acknowledged manpower shortages, noting that the Federal Government was working to recruit more health workers. It explained that recruitment required institutional verification and compliance with established procedures, adding that the hospital was following due process to address its staffing gaps.

Reaffirming its commitment to healthcare delivery, training and research, UPTH urged journalists, partners and members of the public to verify information and engage the management whenever they had concerns. The hospital assured the public of its readiness to respond to inquiries and its commitment to providing professional and quality healthcare services.

item.content:encoded:
Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has been discharged from hospital and is "doing well" following his collapse at the club's training ground.

Kompany, 40, was rushed to hospital last Friday after taking ill as he watched the club's second team train.

The cause has been identified as meningeal irritation - an inflammation of the protective membrane surrounding the brain and spinal cord.

"Given the circumstances, he's doing well," Max Eberl, the club's board member for sports, told German broadcaster ARD on Wednesday.

"He was discharged from the hospital today. That is the biggest and best news for all of us."

No timeline has been set for Kompany's return and Bayern said on Saturday that it would be a matter of "weeks, not days" until the former Manchester City defender returned to the dugout.

English assistant coach Aaron Danks has taken over in Kompany's absence and oversaw a 3-1 win at Freiburg on Sunday.

Kompany had been nursing a virus in the days before his collapse and missed some team training sessions.

The Belgian missed a pre-match news conference prior to Bayern's Champions League game against Arsenal last Tuesday, but was subsequently on the touchline for the match on Wednesday.

"It's a meningeal irritation that caused this incident on Friday. He will now rest and take medication," said Eberl, speaking before Bayern's German Cup tie against Magdeburg.

"I am very confident that he will be back on the touchline, operating at 100% very soon."


Current leaders Bayern face title rivals Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga on Saturday.
